blocks.value: Everything your programs have produced so far vanished the moment they ended. Files are how a program remembers.

This is also the lesson where Lesson 16 stops being theoretical. Nearly every operation here throws a **checked** exception: the compiler will not let you ignore it, so exception handling is no longer good practice, it is a requirement to compile.
What you will be able to do
By the end of this lesson you will be able to:

items: Distinguish volatile from non-volatile storage, and text from binary files
Build and inspect file paths with the `Path` and `Files` classes
Write text to a file and read it back
Choose the right `StandardOpenOption` for a task
